title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Aldia shares some traits with King Allant from *Demon's Souls*. Their voices are very similar, and their appearances are both that of deformed creatures which were once human.
If Aldia manifests to the player at the Shrine Entrance bonfire in the Dragon Shrine, due to the small area where it's located, a very tiny version of Aldia will emerge.
Both of Aldia's tree root attacks are very similar to pyromancies the Bearer of the Curse can find, such as Fire Snake or Firestorm.
Aldia is passively referenced in Dark Souls III, based on the Japanese item description and name (Soul Geyser) for Soul Stream. He may also be the subject depicted in the statue of the "root man" with a book present at Grand Archives.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Aldia is immobile when fought, but is able to teleport, releasing an area of effect attack around the area he teleports to.

Several of Aldia's attacks deal mixed Fire and Dark damage, so some form of fire defense is recommended for this fight. All of his attacks deal either pure physical or Fire/Dark damage. This means that a shield that is highly resistant to both physical and Fire/Dark damage, such as the Rebel's Greatshield, will reduce his damage output greatly.

The Fire Orbs have moderate tracking, so rolling may be needed to fully evade. Forbidden Sun can be cast in any direction, even directly behind him. The Fire Orb and Forbidden Sun attacks can be avoided by rolling, strafing around Aldia or running perpendicular to their trajectory.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: The deformed Aldia is encountered several times by the Bearer of the Curse, to whom he imparts his extensive knowledge on the nature of life. He expresses outrage over the actions of the Lord of Light, who cursed humans into mortality and introduced the cycle of light and dark by linking the First Flame. Aldia's bleak worldview considers mankind as "props on the stage of life", persevering merely through obsession. While acknowledging the merits of the Age of Fire, he labels the roots of this "warm, resplendent" world as a lie, with the linking of the Fire as its original sin. Nevertheless, Aldia realizes that one could wish to inherit this order, even if built on a "tender, exquisite" lie. Instead of submission to the peace provided by the status quo, he offers a third "path"; obscure and unpaved, yet could perhaps ascend the scope of Light and Dark.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Aldia is the elder brother of King Vendrick, and aided his brother in founding the kingdom of Drangleic. He secluded himself in his manor, searching for secrets of life, viewing the Undead as the key to finding it. For his reverence of the Undead, Aldia was shunned by Vendrick, banished to his Keep forever. People who were invited to his manor commonly disappeared and were replaced with malformed beasts. The Southern and Northern Ritual Bands were created by Aldia and his acolytes after cruel, horrible experiments were performed on these people. Many valuable objects came out of Aldia's Keep, including the Sunset Staff, the Spitfire Spear, Soul Geyser, Unleash Magic, and Forbidden Sun.

Through his experiments, Aldia sought to learn the nature of the undead curse, and to shed the yoke of fate. He failed, however, and turned into a monstrosity, inhabiting the bonfires.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin

After that immediately run up to him to land a few hits before his flames go up.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : Aldia serves as a lore-centric character, alluding to a great deal of things in relation to the lore of *Dark Souls II*.

When the Bearer of the Curse has defeated the Four Great Ones and lit the Primal Bonfires he will emerge and guide the Bearer of the Curse towards his brother Vendrick, now a mindless hollow. He continues to appear to the Bearer of the Curse, seeking to learn their intentions and telling them of the nature of the curse and the fabric of their world.

He will finally attack the Bearer of the Curse before they can take the Throne of Want, seeking to test them. When Aldia is defeated, he will ask what the Bearer of the Curse wants: light, dark or something else entirely. If the Bearer of the Curse chooses to reject the throne and leave, Aldia will narrate the Bearer of the Curse's departure from the throne.

 dialogue : With the introduction of *Scholar of the First Sin*, a great deal of lore-centric dialogue was added to the game, changing much of the preconceived lore.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: In *Scholar of the First Sin*, Aldia, the older brother of King Vendrick, hints at a path for the Bearer of the Curse that differs from the one presented to them. If the conditions are met, he can serve as the final boss of *Dark Souls II*, with his fight triggering after Nashandra's; he, notably, is the only boss in any *Dark Souls* game not to die when defeated, and as such drops no souls nor items, with the player instead gaining the option of an alternate ending in which the Bearer of the Curse is hinted to as following this mysterious other path at Aldia's side. He is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III* via the Soul Stream description, which refers to him as "**the first of the Scholars**". He is voiced by David Gant, who also voiced Oswald of Carim in *Dark Souls*.

He was originally only a mentioned character as **Lord Aldia**, a mysterious researcher who conducted horrible experiments in his mansion, Aldia's Keep, but was added into the game proper via the *Scholar of the First Sin* enhanced edition named after him.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
The withered tree branches he utilizes inflict physical damage only, making them especially prone to being blocked. At a distance, the branches extend out of the ground in a path in front of him, with moderate tracking, making it harder to roll out of the path of the attack. This is easily noted when one rolls away from the attack, but gets grazed by one of the branches, yet doesn't flinch or stagger upon getting hit.

Throughout the fight, Aldia will surround himself in a fiery aura that makes close contact with him difficult without the risk of dying to the flames. However, an ultra greatsword can still reach. This aura also bolsters his own defenses, reducing the damage he receives from all attacks by a significant amount. The fiery aura fades when he performs certain moves, giving the player a small window to attack up close. The first opening is just after he teleports to a new location, and the second is when he is charging up his Forbidden Sun attack.

title: Basilisk (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Basilisk (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Ranged attacks are generally the safest way to dispatch Basilisks, as they are unable to attack anything outside of melee range. Care should be taken, however, as they may end up cornering the player and making them unable to escape the Petrification mist. Planning an escape route before engaging a group of Basilisks is advisable.

Basilisks have little to no Poise. This means that they can be stun-locked by almost any attack. Using wide-swinging weapons, like a greatsword, will allow the player to deal with larger groups of Basilisks with relative ease.

They have very little health, even at higher levels of NG+, which means that if they are isolated, players can simply wait for them to discharge their petrifying mist and then flank it.

Being a beast, Basilisks have a weakness to Fire damage. As such, pyromancies and flame infused or buffed weapons will deal considerable damage.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - lead 
 lead : The **Bearer of the Curse** is the player character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls II* and its expansions, *The Lost Crowns*.

The Bearer of the Curse travels to Drangleic by a compulsion to find a way to break the curse of the undead and avoid Hollowing at any cost.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
At the bottom of the gaping hole in Majula lurks things long forgotten. Here, The Rotten, a hideous amalgamation of corpses awaits. After making their way through The Gutter, a place where unwanted things have been discarded, the Bearer of the Curse faces down the Rotten itself in its lair, slaying it and claiming its soul for their own.

After freeing Rosabeth of Melfia from her petrification, the path is now open from Majula to Brightstone Cove Tseldora. The Brightstone Cove Tseldora once housed a prosperous town, grown rich after its founder, the Duke Tseldora, discovered its massive crystal deposits. The Duke was always a peculiar figure however, obsessed with spiders, and one day, a massive spider known as The Duke's Dear Freja and her countless children overran the town, and the Duke was never seen again. Fighting their way to the spider's lair, the Bearer of the Curse slays the beast and finds the final Great Soul hidden in her lair.

 trivia : While not mentioned in the game, according to the official *Dark Souls II* twitter, the Bearer of the Curse for both genders have birthdates; April 8th for the female character, and May 8th for the male character. This was agreed upon by the developers as it represents them well and is a fun additional fact. This extra information is recent and mentioned on twitter after the game's online servers went online.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:

 dragon_aerie : Following the symbol of the King will lead the Bearer of the Curse to Aldia's Keep. Aldia was the King's brother, who sought to create dragons, and has long since disappeared. Journeying through the Keep, home to the results of Aldia's mad experiments, will eventually bring the Bearer to the Dragon Aerie, where they will find the Emerald Herald awaiting them. She directs the Bearer to the very top of the Aerie, the Dragon Shrine, to seek the Ancient Dragon. She claims that the dragon has been watching over the world for aeons, and awaits the Bearer of the Curse.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse fights their way through the knights and defeats Velstadt, finding Vendrick at last. The King, however, has been reduced to a hollow, wandering the grounds aimlessly. The Bearer may choose to put the king out of his misery, or leave him to wander endlessly. Here, the Bearer of the Curse finds the King's Ring, and the Emerald Herald, who tells them that the ring will open the way to the far east, where the Bearer of the Curse must journey next. She proceeds to warn the Bearer that if they continue on this path, they too will one day walk these grounds without really remembering why.

Should the Bearer of the Curse seek her council, Nashandra too will direct the Bearer of the Curse to follow the symbol of the King.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - prologue 
 prologue : The Bearer of the Curse became undead at some point, hollowing until they had no recollection of their former life. Desperate to find a cure, they were drawn to the walled off kingdom of Drangleic, where a cure to the undead curse was rumored to exist. Journeying through a portal and guided by a Fire Keeper, the Bearer of the Curse found themselves in the Things Betwixt. Finding there a hut with the remaining Fire Keepers, the Bearer of the Curse is made to remember more of their past and is cured of their hollowing through a Human Effigy. The Bearer is then guided towards Majula to seek the Emerald Herald.

The Herald, in turn, tells the Bearer of the Curse to seek the king, Vendrick, to find their answers and claim the throne, but warns that the Bearer will never find the king with a soul so pallid, instructing them to seek out the four Great Ones and to claim their power.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:

 the_three_crowns : Should the Bearer of the Curse choose to do so, they may use the Ashen Mist Heart on Vendrick's belongings in the Undead Crypt. Doing so will allow the Bearer to speak directly to the king as he was before he hollowed. Bitter and resigned to defeat, the king will council the Bearer of the Curse, warning them of the futility in seeking fire, of the dark that lies within them, and of the children of Manus, Father of the Abyss. He will tell the Bearer to seek three crowns of power, belonging to fallen kings. He will also warn the Bearer of his wife, Nashandra, revealing that she too is a child of the Abyss.

 undead_crypt : After traveling through the Shrine of Amana, the Bearer of the Curse will come upon the Undead Crypt, a place that has stood since the dawn of time, and where men and gods alike have been interred. Here, Vendrick came along with his loyal knights and his right hand, Velstadt, the Royal Aegis. Many servants of Vendrick have come to find the King, only to meet their end at the hands of the Royal Aegis and the King's knights.

Upon descending from the elevator, the Bearer of the Curse will stumble upon the Scholar once more if met at the last primal bonfire. The Scholar will ask the Bearer if they still desire peace, if answered yes, he will tell them that Vendrick is here and not far off. He will state that the Bearer was neither born with greatness nor granted it by the fates, before once again disappearing into the flames.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse will journey through the Black Gulch to find the fallen kingdom of Shulva, Sanctum City, once ruled by the Sunken King. The king ruled the city, centred around the worship of a slumbering dragon known as Sinh, until his kingdom was invaded by the Drakeblood Knights lead by Sir Yorgh, who sought to claim the dragon's blood. Sir Yorgh slew the king, and awoke the dragon, which proceeded to kill him and lay waste to the city with its poison. The Bearer of the Curse slays Elana, the Squalid Queen, a child of the Abyss, and the dragon Sinh to claim the Sunken King's crown.

Next, the Bearer of the Curse returns to the Old Iron Kingdom, to seek the Old Iron King's crown. Finding the kingdom under the sway of another child of the Abyss, Nadalia, Bride of Ash, the Bearer braves their way through the ruined towers to find the Fume Knight, who guards the crown of the Old Iron King.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Finally, the Bearer of the Curse travels to Frozen Eleum Loyce, once ruled by the Ivory King. Built to contain the Old Chaos, the city was abandoned and froze over when its king vanished into the chaos. Guided by the last child of the Abyss, Alsanna, Silent Oracle, the Bearer of the Curse seeks out the remaining knights of Eleum Loyce to gain their help in braving the Old Chaos. Finding the Burnt Ivory King there, the Bearer of the Curse defeats him and claims his crown.

Once the Bearer of the Curse has found all three crowns of old, along with Vendrick's own crown, the fallen king will unleash the hidden power of the crowns, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. Bidding the Bearer to seek strength, and asking them whether allowing the flames to fade is truly their only choice, the king sends the Bearer of the Curse on their way.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet: When about to light the last primal bonfire, the Bearer of the Curse is surprised by the Scholar of the First Sin, who emerges from the bonfire. The Scholar asks if they want to "shed the curse", unless they have already joined the crestfallen, he tells them that there are two paths: to inherit the order of the world, or destroy it. He admits that very few have come this far, and yet the Bearer's journey is far from over. The Scholar asks of the Bearer to seek Vendrick, "he who almost became a true monarch", for he will guide their way. After this, the Scholar will disappear, letting the Bearer of the Curse light the primal bonfire.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - four_great_ones 
 four_great_ones : The Bearer of the Curse sets out to find the Four Great Ones.

Through the rotunda in Majula, the Bearer of the Curse makes their way to the ancient domain of the Old Iron King, whose hubris led to his death beneath the molten iron, where he was possessed by the soul of one whose name must not be repeated. Making their way through the king's old hunting grounds and the now poison-filled valley surrounding the castle, the Bearer of the Curse finds and slays the Old Iron King, claiming his soul for their own.

By way of ship or on the wings of an eagle, the Bearer of the Curse makes their way to The Lost Bastille, a forgotten prison where the Lost Sinner is held. The Lost Sinner was imprisoned for the sin of attempting to relight the First Flame. The Bearer of the Curse fights their way down into the very bottom of the prison, where they face the Sinner and take her soul for their own.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - giant_memories 
 giant_memories : Using the Ashen Mist Heart on the corpse of the giant Jeigh will allow the Bearer of the Curse to enter the giant's memories and fight the Giant Lord during the final days of the war between Drangleic and the Giants. Upon defeating the Giant Lord, they will acquire the Giant's Kinship which will allow them to claim the Throne of Want.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Once arriving at the Dragon Shrine bonfire, the Scholar appears once more. He will reveal that he is in fact Aldia, the elder brother of Vendrick. Aldia says that he "sought to shed the yoke of fate, but failed" and that he now only awaits an answer. He asks of the Bearer of the Curse to "seek the Throne, seek light, dark and what lies beyond", for the last time, he'll vanish into the flames, allowing the Bearer of the Curse to light the bonfire.

The Ancient Dragon will give the Bearer the Ashen Mist Heart, which allows one to peer into the memories of things long withered. Should the Bearer of the Curse again seek out Nashandra's council, she will warn that the dragon is a false deity and is in fact no more than a prop. Still, she will direct the Bearer of the Curse to go to the Forest of Fallen Giants, to use the Ashen Mist Heart to peer into the Giants' memories.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - epilogue 
 epilogue : ***Proceed to the Throne:** In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse will accept their part in the cycle of the world, and take the throne. Doing so means that they will either sacrifice themselves to link the flame, or allow the flame to continue fading and become the Dark Lord. Which the Bearer of the Curse chooses is unknown.

***Leave the Throne: **In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse rejects the throne, and bitterly walks away, seemingly to seek another, more permanent way to end the curse.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - appearance 
 appearance : In the trailers, artwork, and promotional artwork for *Dark Souls II*, the Bearer of the Curse is depicted wearing the Faraam Set as well as using the Longsword and Spear (dual-wielding) along with the Golden Wing Shield as their main weapons. In the intro video of *Dark Souls II*, the Bearer of the Curse is seen wearing the Imported Set.

In-game, like the Chosen Undead from *Dark Souls*, the Bearer of the Curse's appearance and attributes are determined by the player, including their face/body, sex, origin, starting class and equipment.

Also, like the Chosen Undead, the character's personality is portrayed as an archetypal silent protagonist who doesn't have any sort of spoken dialogue during the game (aside from making some grunts or cries whenever they are hurt or killed).

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - drangleic_castle 
 drangleic_castle : Now with the strength of the four Great Ones, the Bearer of the Curse may pass through the Shrine of Winter to reach Drangleic Castle, the stronghold of Vendrick himself. The Emerald Herald awaits outside, directing the Bearer of the Curse to enter the castle. There is no trace of the King inside the castle however, instead the Bearer of the Curse finds his Queen, Nashandra. Nashandra tells the Bearer of the Curse that Vendrick was less of a king than one might imagine, and that he never took the true throne. She will direct the Bearer of the Curse to the Undead Crypt, to put an end to Vendrick.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet: If Vendrick is defeated before Nashandra, and the Bearer of the Curse has spoken to Aldia in the three mentioned locations, answering yes to both questions asked by Aldia, after Nashandra's defeat, Aldia will appear saying that "many monarchs have come and gone" and requires the Bearer of the Curse's answer as "conqueror of adversities". Aldia will then test the Bearer of the Curse to see if they are truly worthy of receiving the throne by confronting them himself. The Bearer of the Curse defeats Aldia. After Aldia, The Scholar of the First Sin is defeated, the Bearer of the Curse is given two endings.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - throne_of_want 
 throne_of_want : Below Drangleic Castle, the Throne of Want awaits. Here the Emerald Herald will meet the Bearer of the Curse one final time, declaring her journey completed. She warns that if the Bearer of the Curse proceeds, Nashandra, knowing the Bearer of the Curse will link the fire, and coveting the power of the First Flame and the Great Soul, will come for them. She urges the Bearer of the Curse to put an end to Nashandra.

After defeating the Throne Watcher and Defender, the Bearer of the Curse will be greeted by Nashandra, now in her true form, as a child of Manus, Father of the Abyss. The Bearer of the Curse defeats Nashandra.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet:
Belfry Gargoyles -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : **Combo Strikes**: Swings their halberds 3 times in a row 2 doing horizontal slashes and the 3rd performs an overhead strike.

**Flank**: Flies into the air and lands behind the player and follows it up with a lunge.

**Sweep**: Performs a singular sweep, no follow ups.

**Flame breath**: Shoots out a fire breath from their mouth, comes in two forms. One where it is a straight line of fire and the other is a broad sweep of fire.

**Aerial Flame**: Flies into the air and shoots out a fire breath in a wide arc

**Thunderstorm: **The halberd is imbued in electricity, then holds it up in the air and fires off several lightning bolts around the caster.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet:
Belfry Gargoyles -  Dark Souls II - boss - defenses 
 defenses : (Stats are from Param Studio and are not estimated)
Slash/Strike/Thrust defense are applied on top of Physical Defense. -35% strike means taking 135% damage.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet: Attacking an inactive gargoyle before it is supposed to spawn will instantly activate it. It is possible to fight all five gargoyles at once which can make the battle almost impossible unless the player is skilled enough.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet:
Belfry Gargoyles -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia 
 trivia : It is possible to see one of the gargoyles by The Lost Bastille in Sinners' Rise. In *Scholar of the First Sin*, a total of three gargoyles are seen.
Owing to their nature, the Belfry Gargoyles share an identical theme to the Bell Gargoyles from Dark Souls. As such, it is the only theme in Dark Souls II to be taken from a previous game.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet:
Belfry Gargoyles -  Dark Souls II - boss - description 
 description : These gargoyles are similar in appearance to the Bell Gargoyles from *Dark Souls* and even share the same battle music. They wield large bidents.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet:
Belfry Gargoyles -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Two gargoyles are present at the start of the battle. One is on a pedestal to the immediate left upon entering the boss area, while the other is on the right, further away from the player. Distance should be put between the Gargoyles and the player, as this will allow the player to use magic and ranged weapons. The Gargoyles can slash, stab, lunge, and breathe fire at the player. If the player chooses to use ranged weaponry, then all Gargoyles should be within view at all times and the player should exploit the Gargoyles openings whenever they present themselves. Since they can only face one direction and are completely still while breathing fire, it is one of the best times to attack them. The gargoyles are vulnerable to lightning damage.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet:
Belfry Gargoyles -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Belfry Gargoyles** are an optional boss in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet:
Belfry Gargoyles -  Dark Souls II - boss - location 
 location : The Belfry Gargoyles are located in Belfry Luna. One must use extra caution in the short area before the boss, as this is where Bell Keeper covenant players will be randomly summoned to harass and impede the player from pulling the lever atop the tower to gain access to the boss room.

In *Scholar of the First Sin* edition, there is also one Belfry Gargoyle on the rooftop of Drangleic Castle, where an Alonne Knight Captain is encountered. Another is found in one of the side rooms in Aldia's Keep.

title: Belfry Gargoyles
snippet:
Belfry Gargoyles -  Dark Souls II - boss - notes 
 notes : The Belfry Gargoyles can be parried.
By burning a Bonfire Ascetic on the Belfry Luna bonfire, Upper Ramparts, the Belfry Gargoyles can be respawned. A broken staircase will impede a direct path to fight them, however, so the player must first travel to the Servants' Quarters bonfire in The Lost Bastille, and from there take the ladder down and make their way to Belfry Luna again.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Although Lucatiel mostly remains calm and collected, she becomes incredibly distressed with the idea of going hollow and losing all of her memories. At one point, she even claims that she would be willing to kill the player if it meant that she would be able to get rid of the curse. However, in the end, Lucatiel comes to terms with her condition and accepts that she will eventually go hollow.

Lucatiel wields the Mirrah Greatsword and the Mirrah Shield.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
If the player kills Lucatiel, her equipment will be sold by Merchant Hag Melentia, although this method voids the achievement/trophy for that New Game cycle.
Her achievement/trophy is missable. If the player has not had Lucatiel survive at least three fights before speaking to her in Aldia's Keep, she will disappear from the game until the next New Game cycle.
Lucatiel will not go to Aldia's Keep until her dialogue has been exhausted in all other locations. If she is not found at the bonfire in the shack, the player can prompt her to move by backtracking and talking to her in all locations.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - locations 
 locations : Lucatiel can be found for the first time in any of the following locations and she will deliver different dialogue depending on the number of times she has previously been met:
No-man's Wharf: Next to the only bonfire in the area.
**In , she is located in a house further in the area.
The Lost Bastille: In the tower straight ahead when approaching the Lost Bastille from McDuff's Workshop.
Earthen Peak: At the Lower Earthen Peak bonfire.
**In , she is located in the same area as the Poisonbite Ring.
Black Gulch: In a hidden cave. The player will need to drop from the cliff in order to find the cave.
Aldia's Keep: At the first bonfire, after meeting her in all of the aforementioned locations.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet: Lastly, Lucatiel can be found in a shack at the first bonfire of Aldia's Keep. She will be distressed if the player has not summoned and kept her alive for three boss fights, and begs the player to remember her name, as she may not. Lucatiel will disappear from the game after this encounter. If the player has summoned Lucatiel and kept her alive for three of the four summonable boss fights in the base game, she will thank the player for keeping her sane, and bequeath her armor and sword to the player. This is necessary for unlocking her achievement/trophy. In either case, she will disappear from the game as a regular NPC, and her final fate remains unknown, leaving it up to the player's own interpretation.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - notes 
 notes : A player must be wary that the soul reward of beating a boss with the aid of a phantom will be 25% less than the reward from beating it alone. Pursuing Lucatiel's storyline thus forces the player to sacrifice some soul reward as she must be summoned for at least three boss fights. This makes fighting the Flexile Sentry, the Rotten and the Smelter Demon the best choices for summoning her, as less souls are lost (even using a Bonfire Ascetic to fight the Flexile Sentry numerous times is less profitable). The rewards for following Lucatiel's storyline are Lucatiel's Set and the Mirrah Greatsword.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - lead 
 lead : **Lucatiel of Mirrah** is a character in *Dark Souls II*. She first appears as a talkable NPC in four different locations, with her dialogue affected not by the location but by how many times she has encountered the player before; if her dialogue has been exhausted in all four locations, she will relocate to Aldia's Keep for a fifth and final encounter. She can be summoned as a phantom for as many as five different boss fight, with each summon unlocked by one of her five dialogue interactions.

A human knight from Mirrah who came to Drangleic seeking her brother and a cure for her undeath, she is terrified at the prospect of losing her memories and turning hollow. She is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III* via various item descriptions, and is mentioned by name only through her mask's name.

She is voiced by Sarah Beck Mather, who also voiced Irina of Carim in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet: The fourth time that the player finds Lucatiel, she is very confused and distressed over the curse, and says she would do anything to get rid of it, even if it meant killing the player. After exhausting her dialogue, she will be available as a phantom for another boss fight and will move to the next area.

title: Lucatiel's Set
snippet:
Lucatiel's Set -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Worn by knights while on travel. Belonged to Lucatiel of Mirrah.

Only those who have distinguished themselves on the battlefield were admitted into the elite ranks of Mirrah's official order of knights.

It is common to hear of a peasant's dream of striving for knighthood as an escape from hardship, but who would ever think it possible?

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : When Lucatiel is found for the first time, she will introduce herself and explain her motives for being in Drangleic. She will also offer her assistance to the player during their journey.

During her second encounter, Lucatiel will tell the player about her past in Mirrah. She will then take off her mask, revealing her partly hollowed visage, and give the player a Human Effigy, while claiming not to even know what it is.

The third time she is met, she tells the player about her fears of losing her memories and of her brother. Lucatiel will explain how he is a better swordsman than her and she confesses that her brother, who is another victim of the curse of undeath, might be in Drangleic. She then gifts the Ring of Steel Protection +1.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Due to Lucatiel's poor A.I., keeping her alive during boss fights can be difficult. However, the player can equip the Redeye Ring so that the boss focuses its attacks on the player. That way, the player will simply have to avoid the boss attacks while Lucatiel deals damage. Summoning another player is another good way for keeping her alive.
The player can use a Bonfire Ascetic in order to make both the area boss and Lucatiel respawn. It is recommended to do this with the Flexile Sentry, since Lucatiel's chances of survival are higher in this boss fight. Should Lucatiel survive a battle with a boss respawned with an Ascetic, the fight will count for the achievement/trophy.
If the player kills Lucatiel, her equipment will be sold by Merchant Hag Melentia, although this method voids the achievement/trophy for that New Game cycle.

title: Mirrah Set
snippet:
Mirrah Set -  Dark Souls III - armor - availability 
 availability : Set without Lucatiel's Mask can be found on a corpse in a tower along with the Chloranthy Ring in the Undead Settlement. The tower is accessible by dropping down off the rooftop where two Evangelists guard Flynn's Ring.
Lucatiel's Mask is obtained by trading a Vertebra Shackle with Pickle Pee at Firelink Shrine.

title: Lucatiel's Mask
snippet:
Lucatiel's Mask -  Dark Souls II - armor - availability 
 availability : Obtained either by completing Lucatiel of Mirrah's questline or by killing her. The first method results in Lucatiel also gifting the rest of her set as well as her weapon, the Mirrah Greatsword; if she is killed, she will drop only her mask, and the rest of her possessions will be made available for purchase from Merchant Hag Melentia in Majula.

A maskless version of the headwear, the Mirrah Hat, can be found in the Frigid Outskirts in *Crown of the Ivory King*.

It is worn in-game by three separate characters: Lucatiel, the Dark Spirit Aslatiel of Mirrah, and Cerah the Old Explorer, who makes up one third of the Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer boss battle in *Crown of the Sunken King*.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet: After she contracted the curse of undeath, Lucatiel traveled to Drangleic as it was rumored that the cure could be found in this land. With time, she became certain that her brother must have come here too. Lucatiel later confides that she feels the curse is taking over her, and that her memories begin to fade away, starting with the oldest.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - description 
 description : Lucatiel has a rather androgynous appearance, with long, blonde hair wrapped in a ponytail, but her most distinctive feature is the metal bearded mask she uses to cover her face. Lucatiel will temporarily remove the mask after the player has gone through her entire dialogue when meeting her for the second time. This will reveal that although she is still sane, half her face has Hollowed, showing that her body is succumbing to the curse.

Lucatiel is somewhat of a loner and usually prefers to stay away from people. However, she shows great respect and admiration to those who are brave enough to speak to her and is always willing to offer assistance to those in need.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Lucatiel was born into a family of peasants in Mirrah, an unprivileged part of the society of this kingdom. In order to ensure the well-being of her family, Lucatiel and her older brother joined the army. At an early age, she and her brother took up fencing together and, eventually, Lucatiel's skills on the battlefield allowed her to become a knightess of the Order.

Although Lucatiel was a skilled combatant, she was no match for her brother. She claims that her brother was a far better swordsman than she was, as she was never able to defeat him. At some point in her life, her brother disappeared without a trace. Lucatiel thought that he might have fallen victim to the undead curse.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : Lucatiel's summon sign appears even if she has disappeared from the game.
In her concept artwork, it was revealed that Lucatiel's original weapon of choice was a thrusting sword similar to Chancellor Wellager's Espada Ropera.
Initially, when the first renders and screenshots of Lucatiel were revealed, many fans believed Lucatiel to be male. Her actual gender wasn't known until her voice was heard in-game.
Despite her weapon being classified as a Greatsword, Lucatiel wields her weapon like a straight sword.
Director Yui Tanimura revealed in an interview that Lucatiel was supposed to be a Don Quixote-like character and used to be accompanied by the Bell Keeper of Alken who originally had the role of his Sancho Panza. The idea was scrapped and the original face was repurposed as the iconic mask she now wears.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
An invader named Aslatiel of Mirrah later appears just before entering Aldia's Keep itself, donning Lucatiel's Set. Although he might be an unrelated knight of Mirrah, it is possible that he is Lucatiel's brother, given her suspicions about his traveling to Drangleic as well as their names' similarity.

If her questline was completed, Lucatiel becomes available as a summon for the Burnt Ivory King boss fight in *Crown of the Ivory King*, even though it takes place in Eleum Loyce, far from Drangleic. Whether this is supposed to hint at her situation after her final meeting with the Bearer of the Curse is unclear.

title: Lucatiel's Gloves
snippet:
Lucatiel's Gloves -  Dark Souls II - armor - availability 
 availability : They are obtained either by completing Lucatiel's questline or by killing her and purchasing them from Melentia for 5,200 souls.

title: Rosabeth of Melfia
snippet: To have her go to Majula, the player must first fulfill her request to be to given any spare clothing, as her current dress is in tatters. This allows the player to give her any piece of armor they have, and if they do so she will move to Majula, next to the staircase of the village's monument, wearing whatever was given to her. This will also reward the player with the "**Change of Clothes**" Achievement. Once moved to the hamlet, she will offer all of her previous services, but she will also still accept new clothing should the player decide to give them to her. However, it must be noted that any given piece of armor can't be taken back, so one must be mindful of what they decide to give her.

title: Licia of Lindeldt
snippet:
After relocating to Majula, she is seen next to a strange contraption that can toggle the path leading from Heide's Tower of Flame to Huntsman's Copse. Although she claims that the contraption runs on miracles, and that she will activate it for a price, the Rotunda Lockstone she drops states that there is "nothing magical about it" and is purely mechanical. How she came into possession of this item is unknown.

If the player talks to her with 30 Faith, she will gift them with the Idol's Chime and the Saint's Set.

It is implied that Licia is the Nameless Usurper that invades the player in Drangleic Castle and Undead Crypt.

title: Greirat of the Undead Settlement
snippet: Once the player reaches Lothric Castle and returns to speak with Greirat at Firelink Shrine, he will ask the player if they want him to pillage the castle. There is no way of saving him if he is sent to pillage Lothric Castle; if the player wishes to keep him alive, they must refrain from sending him when he asks for permission to go. However, sending him there completes his questline. Upon finding his ashes, they can be brought to the Shrine Handmaid and new items will be added to her stock in addition to those previously sold by Greirat.

title: Mirrah
snippet:
Mirrah -  Dark Souls III - location - lead 
 lead : **Mirrah** (ミラ) is a mentioned location in *Dark Souls II* and *Dark Souls III*.

title: Licia of Lindeldt
snippet: Perhaps the greatest threat that Licia poses is in casting Soothing Sunlight on herself when she reaches 50% health, sometimes repeatedly, which can quickly bring her back up to full health and negate any damage that the player has dealt to her up to that point. This can be especially troublesome if using a weapon with low base durability, as it is possible that the weapon will break in the midst of battle due to being unable to finish the job. If possible, try to gradually whittle her down to just above 50% health, and then build up a full stamina gauge in order to quickly finish her once she tries to start healing herself.

title: Licia of Lindeldt
snippet:
Licia of Lindeldt -  Dark Souls II - character - location 
 location : Licia is first encountered in Heide's Tower of Flame after defeating the Dragonrider, and is next to the Tower of Flame bonfire.

She will relocate to Majula after exhausting her dialogue, down the steps behind Sweet Shalquoir's house, where she can be found next to the Rotunda device that cannot be activated by the player. She can then open a route to Huntsman's Copse in return for 2,000 souls.

If Licia is killed without invasion, Merchant Hag Melentia will sell Licia's armor, the Saint's Set, after the area has been reset (that is, resting at a bonfire).

title: Mirrah Chain Leggings
snippet:
Mirrah Chain Leggings -  Dark Souls III - armor - availability 
 availability : Found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. After defeating Creighton of Mirrah when he invades in the graveyard past the Church of Yorshka bonfire, return to the bridge that leads into Central Irithyll. The set can be found on a corpse in the middle of the bridge where Creighton was first fought.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet: "Drawing Out True Strength" five times is necessary to complete Yoel's questline, which, together with the subsequent Yuria of Londor questline, lead to The Usurpation of Fire ending. It must be done before reaching the Catacombs of Carthus, since if Yoel is still alive when the player reaches said location, he will die the very moment the Catacombs are entered (including in the Settlement if he has not been recruited). If Yoel dies without having "Drawn Out True Strength" five times, or if the player heals their Dark Sigils with the Fire Keeper after she receives the Fire Keeper Soul, the Londor questline will have failed.

title: Lucatiel's Mask (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Lucatiel's Mask (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - armor - lead 
 lead : **Lucatiel's Mask** is a head armor piece in *Dark Souls III*. It is part of the Mirrah Set.

title: Lucatiel's Mask
snippet:
Lucatiel's Mask -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Mask attached to a ceremonial hat. Belonged to Lucatiel of Mirrah.

Normally hats and masks are separate, but these two have been adjoined.

title: Licia of Lindeldt
snippet:
Licia of Lindeldt -  Dark Souls II - character - notes 
 notes : Killing her early in the game will prevent the player from getting the "Gathering of Exiles" Achievement/Trophy.
In combat she uses many miracles, including Wrath of the Gods, Soothing Sunlight and Blinding Bolt.
There is a bug while invading Licia where the player simultaneously kills her the moment she kills the player. In this scenario, Licia will not be found back in the Rotunda Stone room, the Crushed Eye Orb will not activate, and the player will not receive Licia's drops.
Using Bonfire Ascetics at Majula will increase her difficulty when using the Crushed Eye Orb to invade her.
When invading her, the room is compact, which makes the battle harder due to the fact that her Wrath of the Gods can cause a lot of damage and has long range.
Any shield with 100% physical damage reduction can block her Wrath of the Gods attack.

title: Greirat of the Undead Settlement
snippet:
At this point, the player must defeat an area boss in order for Greirat to return safely. The three earliest bosses available to accomplish this are the Curse-rotted Greatwood, Pontiff Sulyvahn, and the Old Demon King. If the player kills Emma they can also defeat any of the available bosses within Lothric Castle, and any boss in Ashes of Ariandel or The Ringed City is also an option provided that they are accessible.

If Greirat dies during this part of his questline, the player can retrieve his ashes from his body located in the far-right corner of the left path in the sewers of Irithyll, surrounded by three Sewer Centipedes. Bring the ashes to the Shrine Handmaid and she will update her stock of wares with those Greirat initially sold, as well as those that he would have sold had he returned alive.

title: Greirat of the Undead Settlement
snippet: #Once Greirat has left Firelink Shrine, the player can tell Unbreakable Patches about Greirat, provided he still has the full Catarina Set. Patches will then leave to rescue Greirat; Firelink Shrine must be reloaded at least once and Patches must be gone from his location in order to trigger the rescue.

The set can be found on a corpse in the middle of the bridge where Creighton was first fought.

title: Melu Scimitar
snippet:
Melu Scimitar -  Dark Souls II - weapon - availability 
 availability : This is given by Laddersmith Gilligan after buying his most expensive ladder down Majula's deep pit, and is also dropped upon his death.

title: Cale the Cartographer
snippet:
Cale the Cartographer -  Dark Souls II - character - questline 
 questline : In order to complete Cale's questline, the player must first light all the fires on the map found in Majula's mansion. This can be achieved by satisfying the following requirements:
Defeat The Last Giant.
Defeat the Lost Sinner.
Defeat the Old Iron King.
Defeat The Duke's Dear Freja.
Defeat The Rotten.
Obtain the King's Ring.
Defeat the Throne Watcher and Defender.
Obtain the Ashen Mist Heart.

These conditions can be fulfilled in any order and once done, the player may then talk to Cale and receive his armor set as a reward.

title: The Rotten
snippet:
The Rotten -  Dark Souls II - boss - summoning 
 summoning : Lone Hunter Schmidt can be summoned for this battle outside the boss fight underneath the Giant shortcut.
**In , his summoning sign has been moved to just before the two Razorback Nightcrawlers.
Lucatiel of Mirrah can also be summoned in the Hidden Chamber bonfire room, but only after speaking to her beforehand. She can physically be found by falling off and landing on a ledge just outside the first bonfire; use a torch to see the ledge clearly. After falling, follow the path to her – it also leads to the raised area with the poison-spitting statues. The ledge that one falls on should not be confused with the later ledge with a door that can be opened with the Forgotten Key (that leads to Darkdiver Grandahl) and the two Giants.
In *Scholar of the First Sin*, Bashful Ray can also be summoned. His summon sign is found near the Razorback Nightcrawlers next to Lone Hunter Schmidt's summoning sign.

title: Sirris of the Sunless Realms
snippet:
Sirris of the Sunless Realms -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : A member of the Blade of the Darkmoon, Sirris crosses paths with the player numerous times as she hunts down members of Rosaria's Fingers. Her true quest is to confront her grandfather, Hodrick, and end his madness.

In addition to being able to summon her, Sirris calls upon the player's assistance during her quest to help combat her opponents.

In a rare occurence, although she is first met in Firelink Shrine, there is no mention that she is Unkindled or meant to support the Unkindled in their journeys, and her presence in the Shrine remains unadressed except for a possible hint that the Shrine Handmaid might be her grandmother.

title: Majula
snippet:
Saulden, the Crestfallen Warrior
Sweet Shalquoir
Rosabeth of Melfia - Moves to the monument from the forest area north of Majula near Benhart of Jugo if conditions are met.
Stone Trader Chloanne - Moves to just outside Lenigrast's workshop after exhausting her dialogue in Harvest Valley.

title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet: Following the destruction of the Bed of Chaos, Quelana appears to have returned to Izalith, or what remains of it, at some point. Within the Demon Ruins, now neighbouring the Catacombs of Carthus, Quelana's pyromancy tome is found on a corpse clutching onto what seems like the petrified corpse of her sister. If these two fossils are indeed those of Quelana and the Fair Lady, it would show that Quelana ultimately ended her self-imposed exile to be reunited with her last extant sister, in the final hours of her life.

title: Sirris of the Sunless Realms
snippet:
Sirris of the Sunless Realms -  Dark Souls III - character - notes 
 notes : At any point in her questline, it is possible to obtain her talisman and set by killing her whenever she appears in Firelink Shrine. Completing her quest beyond defeating Creighton of Mirrah will allow the player access to Hodrick's equipment as well as her assistance in later boss fights.
Offering a Pale Tongue to Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth to deepen devotion to Rosaria's Fingers will anger Sirris and break her questline, preventing completion until the next game cycle. This also applies to any Pale Tongues offered even after she vows knighthood to the player.
**Before game patch 1.05, simply equipping the covenant item or using Pale Tongues to access Rosaria's rebirth services immediately end Sirris's questline.
Once she has vowed knighthood to the player, she will not retaliate should the player attack her.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
** If the questline is being followed, the Londor Pale Shades will be available as summonable phantoms throughout the game; if the quest has been voided, they will invade as Dark Spirits instead.
** If all conditions for The Usurpation of Fire endings have been fulfilled, Yuria will be a summonable phantom for the Soul of Cinder boss fight, as will a Londor Pale Shade.
** Anri has in fact two mutually exclusive questlines; should the player not aim to complete the Londor questline, they can kill the Old Woman of Londor disguised as a statue in the Church of Yorshka to allow for Anri's other questline instead.

title: Reah of Thorolund
snippet:
Reah of Thorolund -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : In Firelink Shrine next to Petrus after player defeats the Capra Demon in lower Undead Burg. She will be here until the player speaks to Petrus or defeats the Pinwheel, both of which prompt her to leave.
In Tomb of the Giants, in the pit Patches kicks the player down to, after the above conditions are met.
In the church in Undead Parish after being rescued from the pit, praying at the altar. She will not appear until the player kills the non-respawning Berenike Knight there.
In a cell in The Duke's Archives if player buys all her miracles before Petrus kills her.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Must not, in the Catacombs, tell Anri of Horace's location : doing so will result in Anri being killed by the hollowed Horace.
Must not kill the Old Woman of Londor at the Church of Yorshka, where, if the questline is being followed, she is disguised as a statue in a corner where several real statues are situated (attacking without killing her will not fail the questline).

title: Morion Blade
snippet:
Morion Blade -  Dark Souls III - weapon - availability 
 availability : Awarded by Yuria of Londor for fulfilling her initial questline, where she tells the Ashen One how Orbeck of Vinheim has proclaimed himself to be the "Lord of Hollows" and asks if they can see into this matter.

The player must then obtain Orbeck's Ashes and bring them back to Yuria in order to receive the sword.

title: Mound-makers
snippet:
Successfully completing an online session will reward the player with a Vertebra Shackle, which can be offered to the altar in the Pit of Hollows to rank up within the covenant. The method of entering the host's world has no effect on what the Mound-maker must do to complete the session.

Further rewards are granted upon leveling up:

title: Stone Trader Chloanne
snippet:
Stone Trader Chloanne -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : She is Blacksmith Lenigrast's daughter, trying to eke out her vocation as a stone trader all on her own as means of escaping the suffocating ambience of her homeland, Volgen. Exhausting her dialogue will convince her to move to Majula outside her father's workshop, realizing her endeavors brought little success, due to the lack of fellow travelers and merchant encounters.

She initially has a limited stock of Titanite Shards, but eventually begins to sell an unlimited amount of Shards, Large Shards and Chunks once the player has met certain conditions in the story. After spending 20,000 souls at her shop and exhausting her dialogue, she gives the player a piece of Twinkling Titanite.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - later_gods_of_anor_londo 
 later_gods_of_anor_londo : Caitha, Goddess of Tears, who mourns the undeserving dead and the loved ones left behind. It is unclear whether she was already a Deity in the original pantheon of Anor Londo, but she was worshipped in Drangleic by the events of *Dark Souls II*, and by *Dark Souls III*, her cult is prominent in the reformed Way of White.
Yorshka, Priscilla's daughter and the younger half-sister of Gwyndolin from another father. She originated in the Painted World of Ariamis, but by the events of *Dark Souls III* has traveled to Irithyll and met her brother, who deified her and made her part of the Way of White's pantheon. It is unclear what she is the Goddess of, although she inherited Gwyndolin's rule of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Emerald Herald -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : The Emerald Herald was originally featured in the first trailer for *Dark Souls II*, where she is seen overlooking Drangleic and gives a feather to the Bearer of the Curse.
Her mixed and unusual heritage is evidenced by her eyes. She has complete *heterochromia iridum*: her left eye is brown, while her right eye, which is hidden by her hair, is purple. The only way to view this is to move so that the camera can clip through her model.
While a child model of the Emerald Herald does exist within the games files, there is no dialogue showing what purpose the child version would have served.

title: Rosabeth of Melfia
snippet:
Thankfully for her, the Bearer of the Curse would find and release her from her horrible state with a Fragrant Branch of Yore. She will be extremely grateful for their help, though greatly embarrassed due to the state of her attire. After a change of clothing provided by her benefactor, she'll move to Majula, in hopes of meeting up with her teacher there. She will begin to wonder if Carhillion hadn't simply ditched her after she first lost track of him, though in truth the old master hoped she was safe and wondered where she disappeared to.

Even should they reunite in Majula, Rosabeth will decide to practice on her own, wishing to see what she can achieve by herself.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Her appearance and background resemble those of the character Lady Oscar from The Rose of Versailles (ベルサイユのばら) by Riyoko Ikeda.
The description of Lucatiel's Mask in Dark Souls III mentions Lucatiel and the Bearer of the Curse, implying that the Bearer kept their promise to remember her name.

title: Mytha, the Baneful Queen
snippet: She was engaged with the Prince of Alken, but he had no affection for her in spite of her beauty and had a secret love for the Princess of Venn. The knowledge of this drove her mad, causing her to enslave the people of her land; Mytha relied on Mounted Overseers and Manikins to control her slaves, and also hired Desert Sorceress of Jugo to lure more people in her domain. She also hired Mirrah's Suspicious Shadows and the Undead Crypt's Grave Wardens to help keep order. The slaves were to dig the land of Harvest Valley, allowing her to consume the poisonous substances that sprouded from the earth, which would supposedly increase her beauty. Instead, the substances only corrupted her and transformed her into a reptilian monster. The frustration of not only failing to obtain more beauty, instead turning into a monster, prompted her to behead all her Manikins.

title: Karla
snippet:
Karla -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : Karla is located in a locked cell in the lower level of the Irithyll Dungeon, in the area with numerous Jailers. In order to unlock it, the player must have the Jailer's Key Ring, found in the Profaned Capital, and then go back to the Irithyll Dungeon once more to free her.

After exhausting her dialogue and agreeing to rescue her, Karla will relocate to Firelink Shrine and become a merchant there. She can be found under the stairs to the left of Andre's smithy. Unlike most Firelink Shrine characters, she has no questline, nor does she relocate after all of her wares have been purchased, and will remain in Firelink Shrine regardless of the player's actions unless killed.

title: Old Woman of Londor
snippet:
Old Woman of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - questline 
 questline : If the player is following either Anri or Yuria's questline, the Old Woman will first appear in the Church of Yorshka in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. There, she will be disguised as a statue via use of the Chameleon spell, where she can be interacted with, ignored, or killed. Killing her or leaving her alive each yield their own consequences.
Should the player leave the Old Woman alive, Anri's questline will end and the Old Woman will next appear outside the Darkmoon Tomb, under Anor Londo. She will present the player with the Sword of Avowal and urge them inside the tomb. Upon using the sword and exiting the tomb, her corpse will lay where she stood, and on it will be the Chameleon sorcery.

title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - complete_ruin 
 complete_ruin : When the First Flame was reduced to a fading spark, the entire world would collapse in on itself, converging toward the Kiln of the Flame and piling up all kingdoms and cities into a massive pile of rubble. In those times, the citizens of the kingdom even forgot the miracles of their queen, the goddess of sunlight, ending up circulating childish but sincere stories to try to recall her image and her blessings. Despite everything, the loyalist knights managed to eliminate the problem of the heretical Winged Knights and the plague of the Pus of Man, however their victory was empty as they too were now reduced to Hollows, consumed to the point of being covered in ramifications and being reduced to patrolling the piles of ruins left of their city. What remained of Lothric's citizens would sink into the stagnant Abyss, becoming possessed by the dregs of the Dark Soul and manifesting as corrupted murkmen.

title: Old Woman of Londor
snippet:
Old Woman of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - notes 
 notes : If the player kills the Old Woman in the Church of Yorshka, Anri's questline will continue but Yuria's questline will end, making the Usurpation of Fire ending unachievable. Leaving her alone causes Anri to be assassinated, ending Anri's questline, but continuing Yuria's.
If the player attacks the Old Woman while she is disguised, but does not kill her, she offers additional dialogue (shown below).

title: Holy Knight Hodrick
snippet: Hodrick is eventually revealed to be Sirris's grandfather and the person she has been searching for on her questline. If the player has defeated the Curse-rotted Greatwood, has assisted her against Creighton in Irithyll, and has defeated Aldrich in Anor Londo, her summon sign can be found outside of the Greatwood's boss arena in the Undead Settlement, where she will finally confront him.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Also of note regarding this questline:
** Giving the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper does not void the questline; if they did so, the player must however avoid summoning her using the sign next to the First Flame bonfire, as doing so will lead to another ending.
** Although it is not recommended as there are no benefits, it is actually fine to kill Yoel after obtaining five Sigils from him; he welcomes this death, and Yuria's dialogue is unaffected.
** Although Yuria requests of the Ashen One to kill Orbeck of Vinheim if he has arrived in the Shrine, this is unrelated to the questline and not necessary to this ending.
** Unlike the other two Pilgrims, the Stone-humped Hag atop The Dreg Heap is unrelated to the questline and can be killed freely without consequences.
** If the questline is being followed, the Londor Pale Shades will be available as summonable phantoms throughout the game; if the quest has been voided, they will invade as Dark Spirits instead.

title: Yellowfinger Heysel
snippet:
Yellowfinger Heysel -  Dark Souls III - character - notes 
 notes : Heysel wears the Obscuring Ring, limiting the player's ability to see her from a distance.
Heysel can heal up via Estus Flask up to two times per encounter.
Heysel will engage other invaders in combat and can take damage from the Great Crabs when she's fought in Road of Sacrifices, though the crabs will never target her directly.
Upon her defeat, the player will be awarded two, three or even four Estus Flask refills.
If the player has defeated Heysel at least once and then offers a Pale Tongue to Rosaria in the Cathedral of the Deep, she will become summonable in the Farron Keep and teach the "Proper bow" gesture.
**As offering a tongue to Rosaria ends Sirris of the Sunless Realms' questline early, and defeating the Abyss Watchers prevents the summoning of Heysel as a white phantom, it's impossible to complete Sirris' questline and learn Proper bow in the same NG cycle.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Must their Dark Sigils with the Fire Keeper after she receives the Fire Keeper Soul (the player Purging Stones or "Request Dissolution" at either the Shrine of Velka in the Undead Settlement or the Purging Monument in The Ringed City); doing so will be perceived as a betrayal by Yuria, leading her to either never appear or rebuke the Ashen One upon their next interaction.
Must not proceed into the Catacombs of Carthus before acquiring 5 Dark Sigils (defeating the Abyss Watchers or interacting with the bonfire which spawns upon their defeat before acquiring the Sigils does not void the questline, but is not recommended in order to avoid accidents).
** Entering the Catacombs will cause Yoel to die, and whether Yuria arrives in Firelink Shrine or not will indicate if the steps were successfully taken. if Yuria does not spawn upon his death, it means that the questline has failed.

title: Archtree
snippet:
Archtree -  Dark Souls - storyline - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the First Flame ignited itself within an Archtree. In fact, the Kiln of the First Flame, which in Dark Souls was covered by the layers of structures in Dark Souls III appears clearly, revealing that the First Flame was stored exactly in the center of an ancient archtree. Additionally, Izalith created her own copy of the First Flame within the archtree at the center of her city, thus in a likely attempt to replicate the original conditions in which the Flame had manifested itself for her experiment.

title: Merchant Hag Melentia
snippet:
Merchant Hag Melentia -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : The traveling merchant Melentia is one of the few survivors of the fall of Drangleic, having witnessed the Giants crossing the sea and the resulting war that lasted for generations. She is always seen carrying her wares on her back due to her experience living in a war zone as one of the poorer commoners. She goes around the long-abandoned battlegrounds in search of things to sell, even stealing things from people in Majula, like Lenigrast. She also seemingly pillages the corpses of the recently deceased, selling their belongings in her shop later.

She speaks of the forest that currently envelops the large, seaside fortress, citing that many believe it to be a result of the dead giants transforming into them upon their death. Though she says not to simply trust the words of an old hag like her, what she says is actually completely true.

title: Eygon of Carim
snippet: Irina's questline can end in two ways: her "good" questline takes place if the Ashen One provides her with all non-dark miracle tomes and purchases the associated miracles. This will lead Irina to finally achieve her dream of becoming a Fire Keeper, relocating to the bottom of one of the towers outside the Shrine. After this, Eygon can be summoned for the Dragonslayer Armour boss fight; once the boss is slain (even if he was not summoned) and Irina has become a Fire Keeper, Eygon's dead body can be found in the cell Irina was originally found. It is unclear how he died, although the fact that he returned to the place he had abandoned Irina might indicate suicide out of guilt for failing to believe in her.

title: Rosabeth of Melfia
snippet:
Rosabeth of Melfia -  Dark Souls II - character - equipment 
 equipment : Note that the armor will change depending on the equipment you have given her. However, this will not increase her defense, as it is merely a cosmetic change.
 There are a few exceptions to this, like the Moon Butterfly Set, which will have her inflict poison on anyone who comes near her, and the Symbol of Avarice, which will slowly kill her.

title: Clandestine Coat
snippet:
Clandestine Coat -  Dark Souls III - armor - availability 
 availability : Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 4,000 souls upon the death of Orbeck of Vinheim. This may happen under **one of two** conditions:
He dies by the player's hand.
His corpse appears in the Grand Archives, which in turn occurs only when **both** of the following conditions have been met:
** He disappears from Firelink Shrine after teaching the player all possible spells.
** The Twin Princes have been defeated.

It is not required to give Orbeck's Ashes to the Shrine Handmaid for her to sell this item, or to even obtain the ashes at all. It immediately becomes available once Orbeck has been flagged as dead.
